explanation: Sized for 5,000 kWh a year plus an EV, in the style of installer 2a8ba8e2.
9.4 kWp is 1.9 kWp per 1,000 kWh of demand; 13 of 15 similar homes got PV, median 9.9 kWp. The roof fits 57 modules, up to 21.02 kWp.
14 of 15 similar homes got a battery, median 10 kWh; this is 1.1 kWh per kWp.
Replaces the gas boiler: 10.5 kW from the heat load (EUR 2,400 heating cost at 12 ct per kWh of heat, over 2,300 full-load hours).
The home has an EV, so a wallbox at 11 kW, the standard size (22 kW needs grid operator approval); 9 of 15 similar homes got one.

assumptions: Hourly simulation over one typical year (Munich PVGIS TMY, pvlib), household load BDEW H25 with single-home scatter.
Electricity 37 ct/kWh, rising 2% a year; feed-in 7.7 ct up to 10 kWp, 6.66 ct above.
Battery 90% usable, 90% round trip, greedy self-consumption.
EV 2,700 kWh a year at 18 kWh/100 km, charged from 18:00.
Heat pump EUR 36,400 less the 30% base subsidy, less EUR 10,000 for the boiler replacement it avoids: EUR 15,480 counted.
Heat pump 5,882 kWh a year: 20,000 kWh heat (heating cost over 12 ct per kWh of heat) at JAZ 3.4.
No feed-in pay in the 573 sunniest hours (negative prices, 2025); upkeep 1.5% of PV and battery cost a year.
NPV over 20 years at 3% discount, 0.5% a year PV degradation, no battery replacement.
PV EUR 1,350 per kWp at 5 kWp falling to EUR 1,000 at 20 kWp; battery EUR 450 per kWh.
